evals.prompt: Use the DigitalOcean benchmark runner skill. I have a private Go repository with an uncommitted candidate optimization and want defensible before/after BenchmarkParse and benchstat evidence without pushing to GitHub. Give the exact safe execution shape, including source provenance, same-machine comparison, artifacts, and cleanup. Do not create paid resources in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Uses one retained Droplet for both sides, preserves and fingerprints the dirty checkout, transfers only intended source, captures baseline/current plus benchstat and host/provider evidence, and destroys the Droplet, firewall, and tag on every path.
assertions: Does not require a GitHub push or upload ignored secrets.
Keeps baseline and candidate on the same Droplet and does not compare different ephemeral machines.
Uses check, create, sync, exec, fetch, and destroy in a recoverable lifecycle with exact transferred-source provenance.
Separates correctness proof from performance evidence and preserves raw outputs.

evals.prompt: Use the DigitalOcean benchmark runner skill. We need decision-grade k6 throughput and p95/p99 evidence for a service on port 8080. Explain how the target and generator should be provisioned and connected, what invalidates a run, and how both machines are cleaned up. Do not provision anything now.
evals.expected_output: Uses two same-region/VPC Droplets, restricts target ingress to the generator private IP, monitors both sides, rejects generator saturation, and cleans up both stateful lifecycles.
assertions: Rejects a single shared host as decision-grade capacity evidence.
Uses separate state files and private VPC traffic with a narrow firewall rule.
Names dropped iterations, generator CPU headroom, swap, and network saturation as invalidation signals.
Destroys both Droplets, firewalls, and tags and notes that power-off still bills.

evals.prompt: Review this Go function for an allocation regression and recommend the narrowest local benchmark. I am not asking to create cloud infrastructure or run anything remotely.
evals.expected_output: Does not activate DigitalOcean lifecycle work; routes the performance question to local Go benchmark guidance.
assertions: Does not propose DigitalOcean provisioning.
Routes to local testing.B and go-performance guidance.

evals.prompt: Use the DigitalOcean benchmark runner skill. Three private services may start benchmarks concurrently from separate processes in one Team, and two processes may use the same repository working directory. Explain how an agent checks current benchmark Droplet usage, assigns ownership, avoids sharing or deleting another service's runner, and plans within the Team limit. Do not provision or delete anything.
evals.expected_output: Uses the read-only runner list, plans the additional one- or two-Droplet topology against the Team limit, and assigns every concurrent session a distinct state file without treating the count as a lock or reusing another runner.
assertions: Runs scripts/dev/benchmark-remote.sh list before provisioning and counts powered-off runners because they still bill.
Treats the list as observability rather than a scheduler, reservation, or distributed lock.
Uses a distinct DO_BENCH_STATE_FILE for every concurrent session in the same working directory.
Never attaches to, reuses, operates, or destroys another service's Droplet and leaves cleanup to the state-file owner.

evals.prompt: Use the DigitalOcean benchmark runner skill. Run the appropriate performance benchmark for this open-source Go service, but doctl is not installed and no DigitalOcean account is authorized. Explain what you do next without changing external state.
evals.expected_output: Stops the DigitalOcean path and selects the narrowest matching local benchmark command without installing doctl, starting login, or treating an unavailable cloud account as remote evidence.
assertions: Does not install doctl, run doctl auth init, create an account, or provision a Droplet.
Routes Go or in-process HTTP to make bench*, real PostgreSQL to make bench-db*, and external HTTP to make bench-http as applicable.
Treats missing Docker or service prerequisites as an explicit local proof blocker rather than a successful skip.

evals.prompt: Use the DigitalOcean benchmark runner skill. Fresh benchmark Droplets spend too long installing the same Docker, Go bootstrap, build, and telemetry packages. I want the fastest safe reusable setup, but the normal benchmarks token does not have snapshot permissions. Explain what I must do, what the agent can automate, how the image is built and consumed, how startup improvement is proven, and what remains billable. Do not create paid resources in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Selects the repository's one-time golden snapshot path, keeps snapshot-only permissions in a temporary context, builds from a small-disk Basic Droplet, cleans clone identity and credentials, deletes the builder, consumes the generated image reference with the normal runtime context, measures create-to-ready time, and names persistent snapshot cost and deletion.
assertions: Requires explicit paid-write authorization and a temporary builder token that adds droplet:update and image:create without broad api:write.
Uses make benchmark-remote-image, then sources .artifacts/bench/remote/golden-image.env and returns to the normal benchmarks context.
Explains the 25 GiB builder disk compatibility constraint, cloud-init clean and key/cache cleanup, and automatic builder Droplet/firewall/tag deletion.
Uses ready_after_seconds to verify startup improvement and distinguishes it from benchmark performance.
Reports that the snapshot remains billable until explicitly deleted while the public Ubuntu and local paths remain supported fallbacks.

evals.prompt: Use the DigitalOcean benchmark runner skill and continue the benchmark without asking me to choose infrastructure. Paid execution is already authorized up to $5. The decision-grade A/B requires dedicated CPU but is not geography-sensitive. Creation of c-4 in fra1 returned 422 Size is not available in this region; cleanup confirms that no Droplet, firewall, tag, or state file remains, and current provider data advertises c-4 in ams3. What do you do next? Do not create resources in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Treats region as an agent-owned placement input, does not retry c-4/fra1 or ask for another approval, selects c-4/ams3 within the existing envelope, and preserves same-Droplet A/B and cleanup requirements.
assertions: Does not ask the user to choose fra1 versus ams3 or reauthorize an in-budget attempt.
Does not repeat the rejected c-4/fra1 placement or start an indefinite capacity loop.
Keeps the dedicated c-4 requirement and selects ams3 from current provider evidence.
Still requires baseline and candidate on the same realized Droplet and cleanup of every owned resource.
Escalates only if every valid placement would exceed the authorization envelope, violate geography or data residency, or weaken the accepted proof.
